evidence.title: President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi
evidence.publisher: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
evidence.claim: The official biography identifies Abdel Fattah El-Sisi as Egypt's eighth president and lists his prior command roles, including commander-in-chief and minister of defense.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary state biography for the incumbent ruler; stable office-identity evidence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to El-Sisi's office and prior military authority; not a claim about nuclear conduct.
contrary_evidence: Biography is self-authored state material and does not by itself prove how he used authority in 2022.

reasons.reason: State biography and office identity are attribution context, not evidence of 2022 nuclear conduct or risk management.

evidence.title: Constitution of the Arab Republic of Egypt
evidence.claim: The constitution text makes the president head of state and executive power, sets a six-year term with no more than two consecutive terms, and gives the president treaty, cabinet, and armed-forces powers with legislative checks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Canonical constitutional text for formal authority and constraints in force in the post-amendment period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Office-level authority, not personal nuclear behavior.
contrary_evidence: Formal powers on paper do not prove the degree of practical discretion in Egypt's political system.

reasons.reason: Formal constitutional powers are useful background, but they do not show how Sisi used those powers in 2022.

evidence.title: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons
evidence.claim: Egypt is listed on the treaty action page as a party to the NPT.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN treaty record for treaty status.
evidence.period_fit: pre-2022 treaty posture still in force during 2022
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level nonproliferation commitment under El-Sisi's administration, not a personal act of command.
contrary_evidence: Treaty membership does not itself demonstrate implementation quality or a strong safety posture.

reasons.reason: Treaty-party status is state posture, not a ruler-attributed nuclear decision or implementation record.

evidence.title: Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty
evidence.claim: Egypt is listed as a signatory to the CTBT.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN treaty record for signature status.
evidence.period_fit: pre-2022 treaty posture still in force during 2022
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level arms-control posture under El-Sisi's administration.
contrary_evidence: Signature is not the same as ratification or implementation; this is a limited arms-control signal.

reasons.reason: CTBT signature is a limited arms-control signal and should not be treated as proof of restraint implementation.

evidence.title: Egypt country factsheet
evidence.claim: IAEA's country sheet lists Egypt's safeguards agreement in force under the NPT.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IAEA legal-status reference for safeguards obligations.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State verification architecture under the Sisi administration, not personal command control.
contrary_evidence: A safeguards agreement helps verification but does not prove comprehensive transparency or a stronger-than-average security posture.

reasons.reason: Safeguards status is institutional context, not direct evidence of personal command, safety, or crisis choice.

evidence.title: Country Details: Egypt
evidence.claim: IAEA PRIS shows Egypt with no operating reactors and four reactors under construction.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IAEA operating-status snapshot for Egypt's civil nuclear program.
evidence.period_fit: stable civilian-nuclear exposure context relevant to 2022
evidence.ruler_attribution: Shows the scope of El-Sisi-era nuclear exposure; it is not a personal-risk choice by itself.
contrary_evidence: No operating reactors means limited direct command-and-control exposure, but also fewer observable 2022 choices.

reasons.reason: Civilian-reactor inventory is exposure context, not a 2022 ruler decision.

evidence.title: Construction permit issued for first Egyptian unit
evidence.claim: ENRRA issued the construction permit for El Dabaa Unit 1, enabling main-stage construction.
evidence.locator: Opening paragraph describing the June 29, 2022 permit
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary national-project authority reporting a dated regulatory milestone.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State regulatory milestone under El-Sisi's administration; not direct proof of personal technical oversight.
contrary_evidence: A permit is a prerequisite, not evidence that operations were safe or that implementation was well governed.

reasons.reason: The construction permit is a project milestone; it does not establish prudent safety governance by itself.

evidence.title: EL DABAA-1 Reactor Details
evidence.claim: IAEA PRIS gives EL DABAA-1 a construction start date of 20 Jul 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary reactor-status database with dated project milestone.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Project timeline under El-Sisi's administration, not evidence of personal command decisions.
contrary_evidence: Construction start is a project activation marker, not proof of prudent safety execution.

reasons.reason: Construction start is a timeline marker, not independent evidence of safety-quality or command discipline.

evidence.title: Construction starts on Egypt's first, Russian-built nuclear plant
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that construction began on Egypt's first Russian-built nuclear plant in July 2022 and that the project was backed by a Russian loan.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a dated project milestone and financing structure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State project under El-Sisi's administration; the financing arrangement is a policy choice but not a direct safety measure.
contrary_evidence: The article describes a financing/project milestone, not independent evidence of safety quality or implementation success.

reasons.reason: The Reuters report is useful project context, but it does not show personal nuclear-risk judgment or safe implementation.

evidence.title: محطة الضبعة النووية
evidence.claim: The SIS page says El Dabaa's first unit had first concrete on 20 July 2022 and describes a core catcher designed to retain molten fuel and prevent release in severe accidents.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local-language official project page with dated milestone and safety-design description; still self-presentational.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State project framing under El-Sisi's administration; not independent verification of performance.
contrary_evidence: This is official project reporting, so the safety description is a claim about design rather than an independent test result.

reasons.reason: Official project safety design claims are self-presentational and should be treated as context until independently verified.

evidence.title: Highlights: 7 conditions must be met ahead of operating El-Dabaa reactors
evidence.claim: EgyptToday reports that operating El-Dabaa reactors requires conditions such as contingency plans, physical protection, safeguards, radiation protection, and radioactive-waste management before operation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Local media summary of a detailed regulatory checklist; useful but not primary regulatory text.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Institutional safety framework under El-Sisi's administration, not proof of personal technical management.
contrary_evidence: The article reports prerequisites, not evidence that they were fully enforced or completed in 2022.

reasons.reason: Pre-operation checklist reporting is a prerequisite list, not evidence that safety conditions were actually enforced.

evidence.title: NPT Review Conference, First Committee: Egypt statement
evidence.claim: Egypt said the NPT had not achieved universality and called for progress toward a Middle East zone free of nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction.
evidence.locator: Egypt statement in the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN coverage of Egypt's diplomatic position at the 2022 NPT Review Conference.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level diplomacy under El-Sisi's administration; not a direct personal speech from the president.
contrary_evidence: Diplomatic support at the UN does not prove domestic implementation or follow-through.

reasons.reason: UN delegation statements on nonproliferation are state-position context, not direct presidential conduct.

evidence.title: General Assembly: Egypt condemns nuclear threats
evidence.claim: Egypt said it condemned any and all nuclear threats, explicit or implicit, regardless of the circumstances.
evidence.locator: Egypt statement in the press release
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN record of Egypt's position on nuclear threats.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State delegation position under El-Sisi's administration, not proof of personal crisis management.
contrary_evidence: A public condemnation of nuclear threats does not by itself prove disciplined crisis behavior or implementation.

reasons.reason: Public condemnation of nuclear threats is diplomatic posture, not evidence of disciplined crisis behavior or implementation.

evidence.title: Sisi: Egypt working with partners to restore peace, stability in Gaza Strip
evidence.claim: Sisi said Egypt was holding contacts with Palestinian and Israeli sides around the clock to prevent the Gaza situation from spinning out of control.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary state statement by the president on an active 2022 crisis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as president.
contrary_evidence: State presentation may overstate Egypt's independent leverage.

evidence.title: Ceasefire Between Israel, Palestinian Militants 'Fragile', Middle East Coordinator Tells Security Council, Urging All Parties to Uphold Truce, Safeguard Past Gains
evidence.claim: The Security Council said Egypt played a crucial role in brokering the Gaza ceasefire and that the effort helped prevent a full-scale war.
evidence.locator: Special Coordinator remarks on Egypt's role
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN confirmation of Egypt's mediation role.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong corroboration of Egypt's mediation policy under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: The same passage notes the ceasefire was fragile and casualties were substantial.

evidence.title: Israel, Palestinians agree truce from Sunday evening - sources
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the truce was mediated by Cairo after an Egyptian security source said Israel had agreed to the proposal.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a negotiated ceasefire and Egyptian mediation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports Egyptian state mediation under Sisi; not direct presidential speech.
contrary_evidence: The report is source-based and does not independently verify the entire ceasefire architecture.

evidence.title: Egypt's President Sisi receives phone call from Ukrainian counterpart - presidency
evidence.claim: Sisi stressed the importance of dialogue and diplomatic solutions to the Russia-Ukraine crisis in a call with Zelenskyy.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a dated presidential call, carried by Euronews.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributes the call to Sisi.
contrary_evidence: A phone call is rhetorical and does not by itself show follow-through.

evidence.title: Egypt calls for prioritising dialogue, diplomatic solutions to solve Ukrainian crisis: Sisi
evidence.claim: Sisi reiterated prioritising dialogue and diplomatic solutions and said Egypt was ready to support that path through bilateral and multilateral contacts.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous reporting of a presidential meeting with Lavrov.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi in a bilateral meeting with Lavrov.
contrary_evidence: State-aligned framing may understate Egypt's balancing act with Russia.

evidence.title: With 143 Votes in Favour, 5 Against, General Assembly Adopts Resolution Condemning Russian Federation's Annexation of Four Eastern Ukraine Regions
evidence.claim: Egypt voted for the resolution and said it wanted hostilities to stop and that dialogue and understanding were preferable to double standards.
evidence.locator: Egypt statement in explanation of vote
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN record of Egypt's explanation of vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State delegation position under Sisi's administration.
contrary_evidence: The UN text is a statement of position, not proof of operational peace policy.

evidence.title: Shoukry asserts Arab Liaison Group's readiness to mediate between Russia, Ukraine
evidence.claim: Egypt said the Arab Liaison Group was ready to mediate between Russia and Ukraine and stressed dialogue and confidence-building measures.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statement on a multilateral mediation track.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State policy under Sisi, though voiced by the foreign minister.
contrary_evidence: Readiness to mediate does not show either side accepted the mediation.

evidence.title: Statement by USG Rosemary DiCarlo - Security Council meeting on the situation in Libya
evidence.publisher: UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs
evidence.claim: UN officials said Libya's constitutional-track talks were held in Cairo, that the delegations agreed on 137 of 197 articles, and that Egypt hosted the next round under UN auspices.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UN account of the Cairo-hosted negotiation track.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Egyptian hosting and facilitation are attributable to the Sisi administration, not to unilateral Libyan decisions.
contrary_evidence: The talks did not resolve all issues and Libya remained unstable.

evidence.title: HoR-HSC Joint Committee Cairo talks end with no agreement on transition or elections
evidence.claim: After the Cairo talks ended without agreement, the UN special adviser thanked Egypt for its hospitality during the three rounds of talks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent local-regional reporting on the talks and the UN's remarks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Supports Egypt's role as host/facilitator, but not as decisive broker.
contrary_evidence: The talks ended without agreement on transition or elections.

evidence.title: Sisi: Egypt did not, will not spare any effort to achieve national reconciliation in Libya
evidence.claim: Sisi said Egypt would support national reconciliation in Libya, back elections as the only way out, and provide all forms of support to that end.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement on Libya policy in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi.
contrary_evidence: Official self-reporting can overstate neutrality and impact.

evidence.title: Sisi affirms Egypt's keenness to provide all means of support to Sudan
evidence.claim: Sisi said Egypt was keen to provide all means of support to achieve political, security and economic stability in Sudan and to continue consultation on the GERD issue.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement on Sudan and regional stability.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi.
contrary_evidence: Support for a neighboring transitional authority is not the same as success in ending the crisis.

evidence.title: Egypt, Sudan call on Ethiopia to actively engage in serious GERD talks to reach legally binding deal
evidence.claim: Egypt and Sudan called on Ethiopia to resume serious talks under AU auspices for a legally binding GERD deal, and Egypt treated unilateral operation as a breach of international law.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local reporting of an official joint statement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Joint statement under Sisi's government; reflects coercive-water-security diplomacy rather than armed force.
contrary_evidence: The wording also shows hard-edged security claims that Ethiopia and others could view as pressure.

evidence.title: Egypt: Investigate police officers, not detainees, for leaked torture videos
evidence.claim: Amnesty says Egyptian authorities responded to leaked prison-abuse videos by investigating detainees and their associates instead of the police officers implicated, and that the videos show detainees with injuries and stress-position abuse.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights investigation with direct review of the videos and follow-on state response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Under Sisi's security apparatus and prosecution system; the report concerns state handling, not a private actor.
contrary_evidence: The Ministry of Interior denied the videos were authentic and claimed the detainees self-harmed.

evidence.title: Egypt: Flawed investigation into death in custody missed opportunity for justice
evidence.claim: Amnesty and HRW say Egyptian authorities failed to conduct an independent, effective, transparent investigation into economist Ayman Hadhoud's custodial death and ignored evidence of enforced disappearance, torture, and ill-treatment.
evidence.locator: Lead paragraph and body paragraphs on investigation failures
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Joint rights investigation with direct sourcing from official records, witness interviews, and forensic review.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to state security, prosecution, and detention authorities operating under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: Officials said the death was non-criminal and attributed it to cardiac causes.

evidence.title: Egypt: Detentions, Repression Follow Protest Calls
evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch reported that Egyptian authorities detained hundreds of people nationwide, and that ECRF documented nearly 700 detentions across 18 governorates between October 1 and November 14, 2022, after social-media calls for anti-government protests.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous independent monitoring with detailed detention counts from a local rights group.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi state and its security services; the arrests were made by Egyptian authorities.
contrary_evidence: Authorities framed the arrests as lawful security action and rejected the rights groups' account.

evidence.title: Egypt: Arrests over calls for protests during COP27 expose reality of human rights crisis
evidence.claim: Amnesty said Egyptian authorities had arrested hundreds of people in the two weeks before COP27 for alleged support of peaceful protest calls, including at least 151 under Supreme State Security Prosecution investigation.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous independent rights reporting with a specific detainee count and legal process details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Egyptian authorities under Sisi's control.
contrary_evidence: The government could argue the arrests were preventive security measures.

evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Egypt
evidence.claim: The report lists credible reports of unlawful killings, enforced disappearances, torture, harsh prison conditions, arbitrary detention, political prisoners, restrictions on assembly and association, GBV, and violence targeting LGBTQI+ people, and says the government did not consistently punish abusive officials.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary U.S. government country report summarizing multiple 2022 abuses and enforcement failures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level assessment under Sisi's administration, not a direct personal act.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes some prosecutions of terrorist attacks and some women being appointed to judicial posts.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: Egypt
evidence.claim: HRW says that in 2022 Egypt continued forced disappearances, torture, flawed mass-trial practices, arbitrary travel bans and asset freezes, prison abuses, repression around COP27, and re-arrest of some released detainees.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: High-quality annual country chapter synthesizing 2022 reporting across detention, prison, protest, refugees, and gender/sexuality issues.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government and security institutions; some items are also structural or inherited.
contrary_evidence: HRW also notes some detainee releases and the national dialogue, but says these did not end the repression campaign.

evidence.title: Egypt: Sexually Abused Refugees Find No Justice
evidence.claim: HRW documented 11 incidents of sexual violence in Egypt between 2016 and 2022 against refugees and asylum seekers and said police often refused reports or failed to investigate, leaving vulnerable women and girls without protection or justice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed investigation with victim interviews and documentation of police failure to respond.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Egyptian police and justice authorities under Sisi; the report concerns protection failure, not private crime alone.
contrary_evidence: The report notes some aid and registration structures exist, but says they did not produce real protection or justice.

evidence.title: Fatal stabbings highlight violence against women in Egypt
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the murder of Nayera Ashraf and other killings highlighted gaps in legal and social protection for women, and that victims and lawyers said police did not always act when complaints were filed.
evidence.locator: Lead paragraphs and case description sections
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a concrete 2022 victim case and broader state-protection gap.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Primarily state protection and policing failure under Sisi, though the immediate killer was a private actor.
contrary_evidence: The prosecution pursued the killer quickly and the court imposed a death sentence, showing some punitive response after the fact.

reasons.reason: Private-actor violence against women is real domestic-safety context, but the link to Sisi is indirect and should not be treated as direct ruler conduct without stronger command or policy evidence.

evidence.title: Egypt: Human rights crisis deepens one year after national human rights strategy launched
evidence.claim: Amnesty said Egypt showed no genuine will to address its human rights crisis and used the National Human Rights Strategy as a propaganda tool while continuing repression ahead of COP27.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights analysis tying official reform rhetoric to ongoing repression in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly critiques the Sisi administration's human-rights policy and messaging.
contrary_evidence: The government could argue the strategy and related initiatives signaled reform intent.

evidence.title: Presidential decree pardoning some prisoners on Eidul Adha
evidence.claim: Sisi issued a decree pardoning a number of prisoners on Eidul Adha and the 70th anniversary of the 23rd of July Revolution, with a security committee to review eligible cases.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official record of a concrete, dated release measure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential action under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: This is limited relief and does not address the broader detention system.

reasons.reason: Pardons and detainee releases are limited remedial signals, not evidence of broad political opening; keep them as minor counterevidence only.

evidence.title: Presidential pardon committee finalizes measures to release 30 prisoners
evidence.claim: The presidential pardon committee said it finalized measures to release 30 prisoners held in pre-trial detention and would keep working with prosecution and Interior to release more detainees.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary official statement on a specific detainee-release action in 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi-backed pardon mechanism and state prosecutorial process.
contrary_evidence: The release of 30 people is modest relative to the scale of reported arbitrary detention.

reasons.reason: A small release action should not be upgraded into regime liberalization without follow-through data on political detainees and protest space.

evidence.title: Sisi declares 2022 as year of civil society
evidence.claim: Sisi publicly declared 2022 the year of civil society and urged state bodies to create a dialogue platform with local and international NGOs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential statement, useful as favorable rhetoric and stated intent.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi.
contrary_evidence: Rights reporting shows that the rhetoric did not prevent arrests, travel bans, and pressure on civil society during 2022.

reasons.reason: Year-of-civil-society rhetoric is programmatic messaging, not evidence of actual tolerance for opposition, media, or NGOs.

evidence.title: Egypt reforms prisons and highlights rights, in moves critics call hollow
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Egypt showcased prison reforms, a five-year human rights strategy, a new rights council, and the lifting of the state of emergency, while critics called the steps superficial and said political prisoners remained detained.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting that captures both official claims and critical rebuttal.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level reform posture under Sisi, with clear limits on practical effect.
contrary_evidence: The same article quotes critics who say the reforms are cosmetic and do not improve detainee treatment.

reasons.reason: The prison-reform story is explicitly mixed and criticized as hollow; it should be treated as contested reform narrative, not decisive democratic improvement.

evidence.title: Egypt: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.claim: The report says Sisi governed Egypt in an increasingly authoritarian manner, that meaningful political opposition was virtually nonexistent, and that dissent, press freedom, and assembly were tightly restricted; it also notes ANHRI suspended Egyptian operations in January 2022 after years of harassment.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual country report with explicit 2022 summary and detailed political-rights sections.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi and his government rather than to a generic country baseline.
contrary_evidence: The report is retrospective and aggregates multiple episodes rather than isolating each 2022 decision.

evidence.title: Egypt: Freedom in the World 2023 Country Report
evidence.claim: In July 2022 Sisi appointed a military general to the Supreme Constitutional Court's first deputy justice post, and the report says the 2018 election was unfair and noncompetitive, with state resources and media used to support Sisi and opposition candidates pressured to withdraw.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Specific 2022 court-appointment detail plus election analysis in the same annual report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Sisi's appointment power and regime entrenchment choices.
contrary_evidence: The report notes the state of emergency was suspended in 2021, but says repressive legislation remained in place.

evidence.title: Egypt still hounding reporters one year after national human rights strategy launch
evidence.claim: RSF said the Egyptian government's systematic persecution of journalists had not let up one year after the human rights strategy launch, with 22 journalists behind bars and more than 500 news websites inaccessible in Egypt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous press-freedom monitoring with concrete counts and a 2022 date stamp.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government and security apparatus.
contrary_evidence: RSF notes that eight journalists had been freed in the prior six months, but says this did not address the structural problem.

evidence.title: Egypt urged to unblock websites and free journalists as part of national dialogue
evidence.claim: RSF said Egypt's national dialogue began with civil society representatives and opposition members, urged the government to unblock websites and free journalists, and noted that 22 journalists were detained at the time.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous report with specific counts and explicit press-freedom demands.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Affects the Sisi administration's handling of civil society and media space.
contrary_evidence: The dialogue itself is consultative and does not prove sustained reform.

evidence.title: Factbox-National political dialogue in Egypt follows years of crackdowns
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the planned national political dialogue was a test of whether authorities would ease a crackdown on dissent, and noted the 2013 protest law requiring prior police approval for demonstrations and tens of thousands detained for political reasons since 2013.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent wire reporting on a ruler-announced dialogue and the surrounding coercive legal environment.
evidence.period_fit: target-year 2022 political environment and dialogue launch
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Sisi's rule because the dialogue and protest law operated under his presidency.
contrary_evidence: The government said the crackdown targeted terrorists and saboteurs, not peaceful opponents.

evidence.title: 2022 Country Report on Human Rights Practices: Egypt
evidence.claim: The report describes serious restrictions on free expression and media, internet freedom, peaceful assembly and association, and political participation, and says the government did not consistently punish officials who committed abuses.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary government country report summarizing 2022 conditions with detailed, structured findings.
evidence.ruler_attribution: State-level assessment under Sisi's administration, not a single personal act.
contrary_evidence: The report also says civilian authorities maintained effective control over the security forces and notes some pardon activity.

evidence.title: Egypt: Human rights crisis deepens one year after national human rights strategy launched
evidence.claim: Amnesty says the national human rights strategy was used as a propaganda tool to conceal repression ahead of COP27, and that authorities censored hundreds of websites, raided and closed independent media, and detained dozens of journalists while thousands remained arbitrarily detained.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed rights report based on extensive documentation and direct engagement with authorities.
evidence.period_fit: target-year 2022 reform narrative and repression record
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly critiques the Sisi administration's governance and messaging.
contrary_evidence: Amnesty acknowledges a positive but very limited release of some prisoners of conscience.

evidence.title: Egypt: Arrests over calls for protests during COP27 expose reality of human rights crisis
evidence.claim: Amnesty reported hundreds of arrests in connection with calls for peaceful protests during COP27, with at least 151 detainees under investigation and hundreds more questioned.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous rights reporting with a specific detainee count and clear protest nexus.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Egyptian authorities under Sisi's control.
contrary_evidence: Authorities also released 766 prisoners over the same period, but Amnesty says arrests outpaced releases and continued to target free speech and association.

evidence.title: Egypt: Detentions, Repression Follow Protest Calls
evidence.claim: HRW said Egyptian authorities detained nearly 700 people across 18 governorates between October 1 and November 14, 2022 after protest calls, and described surveillance and intimidation around COP27.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with local-rights-group documentation and concrete detention counts.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi state and its security services.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes some detainees were released quickly, and authorities framed the crackdown as security work.

evidence.title: International Monetary Fund Statement on Egypt
evidence.claim: IMF staff said the authorities had recently expanded targeted social protection and implemented exchange-rate flexibility, and that continued exchange-rate flexibility plus prudent fiscal and monetary policies were needed to preserve macroeconomic stability.
evidence.locator: paragraph with the IMF mission chief's statement; lines 244-245
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF statement issued contemporaneously with Egypt's reform discussions and directly describing the authorities' actions and needed policies.
evidence.period_fit: directly within 2022 and contemporaneous to the March shock-response period
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to el-Sisi as president overseeing the executive branch, but implementation also depended on the CBE and finance ministry and was driven by the Ukraine shock.
contrary_evidence: The statement describes early steps and policy needs, not proven durable success.
It does not itself show distributional outcomes.

reasons.reason: IMF staff commentary is useful macro context, but it is still a conditional external assessment; do not treat it as completed ruler performance.

evidence.title: Egypt's Economic Update - April 2022
evidence.claim: The World Bank said Egypt allowed the exchange rate to depreciate by about 16 percent and raised policy rates by 100 basis points, while the government introduced a 130 billion Egyptian pound mitigation package to offset price rises.
evidence.locator: Recent Developments section in the April 2022 update
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank country update is a primary institutional assessment; the page summary directly reports the policy moves and their macroeconomic context.
evidence.period_fit: fully within 2022, describing the immediate March 2022 policy response
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to el-Sisi through the executive branch and the CBE, but the actions are also responses to external shocks and central-bank decisions.
contrary_evidence: The same update stresses underlying structural weaknesses and slower growth ahead.
It does not prove that the policy mix was sufficient or well executed.

reasons.reason: World Bank shock-response framing mixes policy, external shocks, and forecast language; keep it as context, not proof of durable competence.

evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
evidence.claim: Carnegie said the Egyptian military had spearheaded the state-led investment strategy Sisi pursued and controlled a vast economic portfolio, including public works, land access, and multiple civilian sectors.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Serious policy analysis with detailed sectoral description and explicit attribution to Sisi's state-led strategy, though it remains interpretive rather than official data.
evidence.period_fit: describes the inherited structure and active 2022 state-led model
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strongly attributable to Sisi as the central executive sponsor of the state-led investment model, though the military and other agencies executed much of it.
contrary_evidence: The paper also notes some practical benefits from military-managed infrastructure and housing.
It is an analytical assessment, not an audited balance sheet.

evidence.title: Throwing Down the Gauntlet: What the IMF Can Do About Egypt's Military Companies
evidence.claim: Carnegie said the IMF had recognized Egyptian military companies as part of the SOE landscape and that many benefited from an uneven playing field, calling for competitive neutrality and stronger anti-monopoly rules.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed policy paper drawing on World Bank and IMF material; the claim is well-supported but still an expert synthesis.
evidence.period_fit: within 2022 and directly about the policy environment Sisi faced
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi-era political economy because it describes the state and military privileges operating under his presidency, though the paper itself is analytical.
contrary_evidence: The paper also notes the government had begun discussing private-sector empowerment and state-asset consolidation.
It does not itself prove that reforms were not attempted.

evidence.title: Egypt's Sisi names Hassan Abdalla as caretaker cbank head
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Sisi appointed Hassan Abdalla as caretaker governor of the central bank after Tarek Amer resigned during the currency crisis, and that Abdalla had senior banking experience and had supported liberal economic policies.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a concrete appointment, with background on the appointee's credentials and policy orientation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as president making the appointment; competence inference is limited to Abdalla's background and market reaction.
contrary_evidence: The post was caretaker/acting, so it shows a personnel response more than a durable institutional choice.
The source does not show that Abdalla changed policy outcomes by itself.

evidence.title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
evidence.claim: IMF staff and the Egyptian authorities reached a staff-level agreement on reforms to safeguard macroeconomic stability, strengthen the social safety net, and underpin private-sector-led growth and job creation.
evidence.locator: press release summary and mission statement; lines 238-251
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF negotiation document naming the authorities' agreed policy package and implementation steps.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to Sisi's government and economic team, though still conditional on IMF approval and implementation by executive agencies.
contrary_evidence: This is a staff-level agreement, not proof of completed implementation.
It reflects IMF conditionality and external pressure as well as domestic choice.

evidence.title: Egypt inflation jumps to five-year high of 18.7% in November
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Egypt's annual urban consumer inflation rose to 18.7 percent in November 2022, the highest since 2017, after the October currency devaluation and continued import restrictions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report using CAPMAS data, with a clear causal chain to policy and supply constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Only partially attributable to Sisi because the inflation spike also reflected external shocks, import shortages, and market conditions, but the devaluation and import restrictions were policy choices of his government.
contrary_evidence: The report itself cites supply shortages and higher production costs, so not all inflation is ruler-caused.
This is an outcome indicator, not a direct policy statement.

evidence.title: IMF Executive Board Approves 46-month US$3 billion Extended Arrangement for Egypt
evidence.claim: The IMF approved Egypt's arrangement and said the package would shift to a flexible exchange rate, reduce the state footprint, level the playing field, strengthen governance and transparency, and expand social spending.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF approval statement describing the agreed policy package and the rationale for it.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to Sisi's government as the borrower-side authority, but conditioned by IMF approval and implementation by the CBE, cabinet, and state agencies.
contrary_evidence: It is a program approval, not proof of implementation success by year-end.
It reflects external conditionality as well as domestic initiative.

evidence.title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
evidence.claim: The World Bank said Egypt faced a spike in inflation and large portfolio outflows, foreign-exchange buffers had fallen since March 2022, growth would slow, poverty could rise, and education spending remained at 2 percent of GDP for FY2022/23.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank country monitor with explicit 2022 macro, poverty, and education-budget discussion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Sisi's government through fiscal and exchange-rate choices, but heavily constrained by the Russia-Ukraine war and global financial tightening.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes that the government announced social mitigation packages and support from the IMF program.
It does not isolate ruler choice from external shocks.

reasons.reason: The year-end monitor is an outcome-and-forecast summary with major external drivers; it should not be read as clean ruler attribution.

evidence.title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt's Flagship Social Protection Program
evidence.claim: The World Bank announced new financing to expand Takaful and Karama, which as of June 2022 covered 3.69 million households; women were 74 percent of beneficiaries and 67 percent of the cash went to Upper Egypt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with direct program coverage and distribution details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government's social-protection apparatus, though the program was co-financed and shaped with the World Bank.
contrary_evidence: This shows mitigation and targeting, not a full answer to broad inequality or labor-market weakness.
It does not prove that the poor were adequately protected from inflation.

evidence.title: Readout from World Bank Group President David Malpass's Meeting with President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi of Egypt
evidence.claim: The World Bank readout said Malpass and Sisi discussed the latest currency devaluation, the effects of the Russian invasion of Ukraine, energy and fertilizer shortages, rising food prices, and the importance of well-targeted cash transfers; Malpass also welcomed Egypt's recent State Ownership Policy and SOE reforms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank readout from a head-of-state meeting, with direct references to policy priorities and macro shocks.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as the president in the meeting, but still framed by external shocks and partner conditionality.
contrary_evidence: A readout is diplomatic context rather than a detailed implementation audit.
It does not show how much reform was actually delivered by year-end.

reasons.reason: A diplomatic readout of macro concerns and policy priorities is context, not a measured implementation audit.

evidence.title: Egypt lifts import curbs, backs bigger private sector role to meet IMF demands
evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Egypt lifted a key import restriction and that President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi approved a list of 62 economic activities the state would leave to the private sector to meet IMF conditions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting on a concrete policy move and a presidential approval tied to IMF conditions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Sisi as the president approving the list and to his government implementing the import-policy reversal; IMF conditionality and the dollar shortage were major external constraints.
contrary_evidence: The move was reactive and tied to IMF demands rather than an autonomous reform agenda.
The article notes continuing foreign-currency shortages and earlier devaluations.

evidence.title: US$ 500 Million Project Will Help to Strengthen Egypt's Food and Nutrition Security
evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a US$500 million project to keep poor and vulnerable Egyptian households supplied with bread, cushion Ukraine-war price shocks, and support food-security reforms; it tied the project to Egypt's Bread Subsidy Program and about one month of wheat supply for roughly 70 million low-income Egyptians, including about 31 million people under the poverty line.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous World Bank press release with specific project terms, beneficiary counts, and policy rationale.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sisi government as the borrower-side authority and policy sponsor, though the shock context was heavily external.
contrary_evidence: The project is a response to crisis pressure, not proof of structural welfare improvement by year-end.
The same text emphasizes pandemic and Ukraine-war shocks.

evidence.title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt's Flagship Social Protection Program
evidence.claim: The World Bank announced US$500 million to expand Egypt's Takaful and Karama program, saying it covered 3.69 million households as of June 2022, that women were 74 percent of card holders/direct beneficiaries, and that 67 percent of the cash went to Upper Egypt.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank press release with direct coverage, targeting, and distribution details.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi government as the policy sponsor, though co-designed with the World Bank and focused on implementation through the Ministry of Social Solidarity.
contrary_evidence: This shows mitigation and targeting, not a full answer to poverty or labor-market weakness.
It does not prove that vulnerable households were adequately protected from inflation.

evidence.title: Protecting and Fulfilling the Rights of Children In Egypt
evidence.claim: UNICEF said poverty had risen despite government programmes, nearly 30 percent of Egyptians lived in monetary poverty, children in poorer backgrounds faced a triple burden of malnutrition, and at least 1 million school-age children with disabilities were out of school along with many refugee and migrant children.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country report is a strong local synthesis, but it is retrospective and not a direct audit of Sisi's personal choices in 2022.
evidence.period_fit: retrospective on the 2022 period and the immediate surrounding years
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level welfare context and criticism of government performance; attribution to Sisi is indirect through national policy responsibility.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes progress in mothers' and children's health and government programmes to expand basic services.
It is a retrospective synthesis, not a year-end implementation audit.

reasons.reason: Retrospective UNICEF synthesis is useful for context, but it is not a direct audit of Sisi-era 2022 social-welfare choices.

evidence.title: Recovering from COVID-19 Learning Losses
evidence.claim: UNICEF said marginalized children, especially migrant and refugee children, were below expected learning levels in literacy and numeracy after COVID-19, and that UNICEF was working with Egypt's education ministry and partners to reach close to 30,000 children with a remediation programme and assessment tools.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UNICEF country story with explicit Egypt-specific remedial action and target group descriptions.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the national education system under the Sisi government, but the remedial action was jointly implemented with UNICEF and external donors.
contrary_evidence: The story emphasizes learning loss and unequal access rather than a completed recovery.
It is a program description, not a final outcome evaluation.

evidence.title: Egypt (EGY) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality
evidence.claim: UNICEF's Egypt country dashboard reports 2022 primary-school attendance at 97 percent and primary completion at 91 percent, with lower-secondary attendance at 85 percent and upper-secondary attendance at 70 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country dashboard is a primary indicator source; the values are directly visible on the page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome context only; not a direct ruler-action measure.
contrary_evidence: High attendance does not eliminate quality or completion gaps for poorer and marginalized children.
The page does not isolate Sisi's personal contribution.

reasons.reason: Indicator dashboard values are country context, not ruler-specific action or attribution evidence.

evidence.title: Egypt (EGY) - Demographics, Health & Infant Mortality
evidence.claim: UNICEF's Egypt country dashboard reports 2022 safely managed drinking-water access at 79 percent and safely managed sanitation access at 57 percent.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country dashboard is a primary indicator source; the values are directly visible on the page.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome context only; not a direct ruler-action measure.
contrary_evidence: The dashboard is outcome data, so it cannot isolate Sisi's personal contribution.
Significant gaps remain, especially in sanitation.

reasons.reason: WASH coverage figures describe outcomes, but they do not isolate 2022 presidential or cabinet decisions.

evidence.title: Child-Related SDG Progress Assessment for Egypt
evidence.claim: UNICEF's child-SDG dashboard for Egypt reports 3 percent of children in extreme poverty in 2022, 33 percent of children below the national poverty line in 2017, and 14 percent child-population coverage by social protection floors/systems in 2020.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF country dashboard is a primary indicator source with direct visible values and methodology context.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-level outcome context only; useful mainly for identifying residual deprivation and limited coverage, not direct personal action.
contrary_evidence: The page mixes different reference years and cannot by itself measure 2022 ruler performance.
It does not separate national policy effects from inherited trends.

reasons.reason: Mixed-period child-poverty and social-protection coverage should be treated as welfare context, not direct performance proof.

evidence.title: WHO Egypt and Ministry of Health and Population celebrate physicians on Family Doctor Day
evidence.claim: WHO and Egypt's Ministry of Health held a 2022 conference for 200 primary health-care workers and said family physicians are the first point of contact for essential care and health emergencies, while WHO continued technical and capacity-building support for family medicine.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous WHO country-office report on a concrete 2022 event and support activity.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Ministry of Health under the Sisi government, though the source also reflects WHO and USAID support.
contrary_evidence: A conference and training support do not prove system-wide service quality.
The source emphasizes staffing shortages and the need for further investment.

evidence.title: WHO Egypt works towards improving the hospital sector in Egypt
evidence.claim: WHO said it worked with Egyptian health authorities in August 2022 to develop the national strategic plan for the hospital sector, and that Egypt was taking active steps to implement universal health insurance and build a more resilient health system.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous WHO country-office report describing a specific policy workshop and the government's UHI implementation direction.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the Sisi-era health ministry and linked institutions, though implementation was collaborative with WHO and higher-education bodies.
contrary_evidence: The source is a workshop report, not an outcome evaluation.
It notes system-development challenges rather than completed reform.

evidence.title: Health systems strengthening towards universal health coverage
evidence.claim: WHO said it actively supported Egypt's Ministry of Health in pursuing universal health coverage and described Egypt's health system as fragmented, with unequal access and large out-of-pocket burdens, while arguing that an equity-driven health sector can help break the illness-poverty cycle.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO country programme page is a strong institutional source, but it is general background rather than a 2022 event report.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Country-system context rather than a discrete Sisi action, though it addresses the system his government governed.
contrary_evidence: The page is framed as long-run support and baseline context, not a year-specific performance audit.
It does not measure 2022 delivery.

reasons.reason: WHO system-strengthening background is baseline context; it should not be used as a direct 2022 output measure.

evidence.title: Improving Wastewater Services Program - Upper Egypt
evidence.claim: Egypt signed a CHF 7.2 million grant on 10 February 2022 for an Aswan water project under SDG 6, with related goals of good health and reduced inequalities.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official ministry project page with a dated financing agreement and explicit location/objective information.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the Sisi government through its international-cooperation ministry, though the project was donor-financed and locally implemented.
contrary_evidence: The page gives project metadata rather than completion or impact results.
It is a grant announcement, not an implementation audit.

evidence.title: Sustainable Rural Sanitation Services Program for Egypt
evidence.claim: The World Bank said its rural sanitation program for Egypt aimed to increase access to and services of rural sanitation in Beheira, Dakahliya, and Sharkiya, improving citizens' well-being and protecting agricultural soil.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Dated World Bank project infographic with explicit geography and objective.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributable to the broader Sisi-era state program and its development partners, not to a single ministerial decision.
contrary_evidence: The infographic is a goal statement, not proof of finished service expansion in 2022.
It does not quantify completed households or outcomes.

evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
evidence.claim: The Egyptian military spearheaded the state-led investment strategy pursued under Sisi and controlled a vast economic portfolio spanning infrastructure, housing, industrial zones, media, and land/import approvals.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Detailed analytic paper with explicit sourcing and concrete institutional description.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and describing the Sisi model operating through 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to Sisi's presidency and the military apparatus he empowered; it shows policy and network control, but not personal enrichment by itself.
contrary_evidence: The same paper notes military-managed infrastructure and low-income housing can deliver some public goods.

reasons.reason: Military-economy analysis is strong on structural opacity, but it is not by itself direct proof of Sisi's personal honesty, assets, or enrichment.

evidence.title: Retain, Restructure, or Divest? Policy Options for Egypt's Military Economy
evidence.claim: Military financial details were kept behind a firewall; the military's costs were described as opaque and based on privileged access to land, contracts, tax and customs exemptions, and conscript labor, while senior retirees in civilian posts reproduced favoritism and patronage.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Analytic paper ties opacity and patronage to named institutional mechanisms and cites IMF and prior research.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and directly relevant to the 2022 economic structure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct to the presidentially backed military economic model; this supports network privilege and concealment, though not a documented personal-family windfall.
contrary_evidence: The military and government claimed cheaper public goods and development value for some projects.

reasons.reason: Institutional opacity and favoritism describe the network environment; they should not be converted into personal self-dealing without asset or procurement evidence tied to Sisi.

evidence.title: Egypt: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
evidence.claim: President Sisi and the security apparatus dominate policymaking, the Administrative Control Authority is under Sisi's control and lacks credibility, transparency, and impartiality, and the government provides very little transparency about spending and operations.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Major country report with direct institutional findings and consistent with other monitoring sources.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong attribution to Sisi because the report explicitly places the ACA and policymaking under his control; it does not prove his private enrichment.
contrary_evidence: The report still acknowledges formal anticorruption mechanisms and state institutions, even though it says they are weak and ineffective.

reasons.reason: A country report on weak transparency is useful context, but it does not establish a ruler-specific integrity finding on its own.

evidence.title: Egypt: Human rights crisis deepens one year after national human rights strategy launched
evidence.claim: The National Human Rights Strategy was drafted without consultation with independent human rights organizations or public engagement, and Amnesty says authorities used it as propaganda to conceal growing repression ahead of COP27 while blaming security threats, economic challenges, and citizens for the rights crisis.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct contemporary rights reporting based on on-the-ground monitoring and a named report.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about a 2022 strategy and repression surrounding COP27.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Attributed to the authorities under Sisi's rule and to a strategy launched under his auspices; it does not prove his personal knowledge of every false or misleading element.
contrary_evidence: Authorities did launch a formal strategy and presented it publicly as a rights commitment.

reasons.reason: Claims about a propaganda-laden rights strategy are relevant to honesty only as indirect evidence of concealment, not as a direct false-statement or financial-abuse finding.

evidence.title: World Report 2023: Egypt
evidence.claim: Sisi declared 2022 the year of civil society, but civil society members still faced arbitrary travel bans, asset freezes, and criminal investigations in retaliation for activism, and thousands remained unjustly detained for peaceful activism.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Annual rights report summarizing 2022 events with a stable country chapter and consistent sourcing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to the government Sisi led; it shows retaliation and continued coercive control rather than personal financial gain.
contrary_evidence: HRW notes some detainees were released in piecemeal fashion, but says repression continued.

reasons.reason: Retrospective repression reporting belongs primarily to 3B and 4B; it is only weakly probative of personal honesty unless tied to a direct concealment or self-benefit nexus.

evidence.title: Factbox-National political dialogue in Egypt follows years of crackdowns
evidence.claim: Reuters reports that Sisi said Egypt holds no political prisoners and that human rights are promoted by jobs and housing, while rights groups estimated tens of thousands detained; the same factbox notes the 2013 protest law banned protests without prior police approval.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters dispatch with direct quotation and contemporaneous contrast to human-rights reporting.
evidence.period_fit: Published in 2022 and discussing the 2022 dialogue and Sisi's public line.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct because the no-political-prisoners claim is Sisi's own statement; the protest-law context is state action under his rule.
contrary_evidence: Egyptian officials said the crackdown targeted terrorists and saboteurs, not political opponents.

evidence.title: Militarizing the Supreme Constitutional Court
evidence.claim: For the first time, an Armed Forces officer was appointed to Egypt's highest court; military judiciary head Salah al-Ruwainy was sworn in as Supreme Constitutional Court first deputy justice.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent Egyptian outlet reporting a clearly identified presidential appointment with date and institutional detail.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable because it followed a presidential appointment; it indicates politicization of a neutral institution, though not personal enrichment.
contrary_evidence: The article does not show personal financial self-dealing, only institutional militarization.

reasons.reason: A militarized court appointment shows politicization, but not personal enrichment or a direct honesty finding.

evidence.title: President El-Sisi Appoints Major General Amr Adel as Chairman of Administrative Control Authority
evidence.publisher: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
evidence.claim: Sisi appointed Major General Amr Adel Ali Hosni as acting head of the Administrative Control Authority, the state's leading anti-corruption body.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential notice of the appointment with exact date and office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment; it suggests control over anti-graft oversight but does not prove a specific corrupt act by Sisi himself.
contrary_evidence: The source does not show what Amr Adel did after appointment or whether the body later acted independently.

reasons.reason: Control over the anti-corruption body is important governance context, but without follow-on conduct it does not prove a personal integrity breach.

evidence.title: New head of Egypt's Supreme Constitutional Court sworn in before Sisi
evidence.claim: Sisi issued a decree appointing Boulos Fahmy Eskandar, a long-serving judge, as head of the Supreme Constitutional Court from the pool of longest-serving deputy chairs.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Mainstream Egyptian outlet reporting a formal judicial appointment with institutional detail and career history.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential appointment under a formal selection rule; this is a counterexample of a professional, non-kin appointment, but one case does not establish a broad pattern.
contrary_evidence: The article also notes the president has appointment authority, so the process still reflects executive influence.

evidence.title: Egypt: IMF Reaches Staff-Level Agreement on an Extended Fund Facility Arrangement
evidence.claim: The IMF said Egypt's program would strengthen governance, accountability, and transparency, reduce the state footprint, adopt a more robust competition framework, and expand targeted social transfers and spending on social assistance, health, and education.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF press release describing the authorities' policy package and conditional reforms.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about 2022 reform negotiations and the 2022 policy package.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect: this is an IMF-supported program negotiated with the authorities, so it shows policy direction and external pressure more than personal integrity by itself.
contrary_evidence: The need for IMF support and the reform conditions themselves indicate that stronger transparency and governance were not yet established practice.

reasons.reason: The IMF governance package is conditional reform context, not evidence that Sisi personally lied, self-dealt, or obstructed scrutiny.

evidence.title: President Sisi approves State Ownership Policy Document
evidence.claim: Sisi approved a state ownership policy document that set a three-year plan to expand private-sector participation from 30 percent to 65 percent, withdraw from 62 business activities, and announce the state's reasoning at each step.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Mainstream report on an official policy document with concrete sectoral targets and implementation rules.
evidence.period_fit: Directly about a 2022 presidential policy decision.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct presidential approval, but implementation was still gradual and subject to strategic-security exceptions, so the document is commitment evidence rather than proof of practice.
contrary_evidence: The same article says the policy would be implemented gradually and that strategic/security considerations could limit withdrawal.

reasons.reason: The state-ownership policy is a commitment document; it should not be overread as actual integrity performance without implementation evidence.

evidence.title: Egypt Economic Conference 2022
evidence.publisher: Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt
evidence.claim: Sisi opened Egypt Economic Conference 2022 and framed the country’s situation as requiring clear and decisive measures to address a decade-long economic and social crisis
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official presidential page is authoritative for what Sisi launched and said, but the language is broad and rhetorical rather than proof of execution.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and about the ruler's stated program.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Strong for program articulation because the page records Sisi's own event and framing; weaker for implementation because the statement is programmatic rather than operational.
contrary_evidence: Rhetorical framing alone does not show actual delivery or durable reform.

reasons.reason: The economic conference page is program articulation, not implementation or outcome evidence.

evidence.title: Egypt's Economic Update - April 2022
evidence.claim: Egypt allowed the exchange rate to depreciate and raised policy rates, while the government introduced a LE130 billion mitigation package that expanded cash transfers and other relief measures
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank is a strong independent macro source, and the page gives specific policy actions and dates.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to the ruler-period macro response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: the measures were taken by the CBE and government under Sisi's political authority, but external shocks and some central-bank autonomy limit personal attribution.
contrary_evidence: Global price shocks and Ukraine-war spillovers were major drivers of the crisis, so outcome attribution is incomplete.

reasons.reason: Macro adjustment and mitigation are relevant, but they are still partly shock-driven and should be contextualized rather than treated as clean execution proof.

evidence.title: US$ 500 Million Project Will Help to Strengthen Egypt's Food and Nutrition Security
evidence.claim: The World Bank approved a $500 million project to keep poor and vulnerable Egyptian households supplied with bread, cushion Ukraine-war price shocks, and support reforms to strengthen food security and nutrition
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The project announcement is explicit, dated, and operational, with a clear target population and financing amount.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and responsive to an external shock during the ruler-period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the project supports a government bread-subsidy and food-security response, but the financing and implementation are shared with the World Bank.
contrary_evidence: The project addresses an external shock and donor-financed support, so it does not by itself prove domestic administrative competence.

reasons.reason: The food-security project is useful implementation context, but donor-financed support and external-shock response make it weaker as a standalone competence proof.

evidence.title: New World Bank Financing Will Expand and Strengthen Egypt's Flagship Social Protection Program
evidence.claim: The World Bank announced $500 million to expand Takaful and Karama, which covered 3.69 million households as of June 2022 and sent most cash to Upper Egypt, while the government expanded social safety nets to absorb price shocks
evidence.source_confidence_reason: The page provides concrete coverage, distribution, and funding details for a named social-protection program.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within 2022 and tied to late-year crisis response and policy follow-through.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate to strong: the government is an implementing partner and the program expansion is an identifiable state action, though the World Bank remains a co-financier and some design predates 2022.
contrary_evidence: The press release is partly World Bank framing and does not independently verify full on-the-ground delivery by year-end.

reasons.reason: The social-protection expansion shows follow-through, but it is still co-financed and not a full year-end implementation audit.

evidence.title: Egypt Economic Monitor, December 2022: Strengthening Resilience through Fiscal and Education Sectors Reforms
evidence.claim: Egypt faced a spike in inflation and large portfolio outflows; foreign exchange buffers fell sharply since March 2022; the CBE allowed the exchange rate to depreciate and raised rates; the government announced social mitigation packages; growth was expected to slow and poverty could rise
evidence.source_confidence_reason: This is a detailed World Bank country monitor with specific macro indicators and policy responses, but it still reflects a forecast environment under external shocks.
evidence.period_fit: Directly late-2022 and contemporaneous with the target period.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the macro deterioration is partly external, but the policy response is attributable to the authorities under Sisi.
contrary_evidence: The report emphasizes that the Russia-Ukraine war, supply-chain disruptions, and tightening global conditions were major drivers, limiting clean ruler attribution.

reasons.reason: The World Bank monitor is a mixed macro snapshot; it is best read as outcome context plus attribution caveat, not as direct proof of program failure or success.

chapter_notes.RECON:
Using the local structured facts as priors, I kept this to a small cross-chapter set and did not re-pull the structured datasets already represented there.

**Core Findings**
- In 2022, Abdel Fattah el-Sisi was Egypt’s president and the formal head of state and executive power.
- The constitutional text gave the presidency significant agenda-setting and appointment power, but those formal checks did not translate into strong practical constraints in the rights/reporting record.
- The biggest inherited conditions in 2022 were the Ukraine-war shock to wheat and FX, long-running macro fragility, demographic pressure, and a weak civil-liberties environment.
- The most useful narrative events for chapter work are: the wheat shock and pound devaluation in spring 2022, El-Dabaa nuclear construction in July, the economic conference in October, COP27 in November, the protest-arrest wave around COP27, and the IMF deal in December.

**Retained Sources**
1. [President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi](https://www.presidency.eg/en/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A6%D8%A7%D8%B3%D8%A9/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D8%A6%D9%8A%D8%B3/) - Presidency of the Arab Republic of Egypt, n.d. Precise fact: official biography identifies El-Sisi as Egypt’s eighth president. Period fit: office/identity anchor for 2022. Ruler attribution: direct official self-presentation. Limitations: self-authored, not independent. Contrary points: none on the page, so use only for identity and tenure.

2. [President of the Republic](https://www.parliament.gov.eg/Constitution.aspx) - Parliament of Egypt, current online constitutional text. Precise fact: articles 139, 140, 147, and 150 define the president as head of state and executive power, with six-year terms, limited consecutive terms, government-reshuffle authority, and joint state-policy setting with the cabinet. Period fit: formal authority and constraint frame in force in 2022. Ruler attribution: office-level legal authority, not personal behavior. Limitations: law-on-the-books only. Contrary points: does not show how much power was actually usable in practice.

3. [Construction permit issued for first Egyptian unit](https://nppa.gov.eg/News/Details?id=570) - Nuclear Power Plants Authority, July 1, 2022. Precise fact: ENRRA granted construction permission for El Dabaa unit 1, enabling main-stage construction. Period fit: 1B capability context in mid-2022. Ruler attribution: state nuclear decision under the Sisi administration. Limitations: official and optimistic. Contrary points: says nothing about operational readiness or broader governance quality.

4. [Ukraine crisis throws Egypt's wheat purchases into doubt](https://uk.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/ukraine-crisis-throws-egypts-wheat-purchases-into-doubt-2597713) - Reuters, March 3, 2022. Precise fact: Russia’s invasion disrupted Egyptian wheat cargoes and pushed prices up; Egypt is a major wheat importer. Period fit: inherited food-security shock at the start of 2022. Ruler attribution: external shock hitting the Sisi government. Limitations: immediate market disruption, not full policy diagnosis. Contrary points: does not by itself establish domestic mismanagement.

5. [Egypt devalues currency 14% after Ukraine war prompts dollar flight](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/egyptian-pound-drops-11-after-ukraine-war-prompts-dollar-flight-2788414) - Reuters, March 21, 2022. Precise fact: Egypt devalued the pound after war-related capital flight and FX pressure. Period fit: macro stress and policy constraint in 2022. Ruler attribution: macro policy under Sisi’s administration. Limitations: one-day news snapshot, not a full macro model. Contrary points: can also be read as an adjustment to inherited imbalances, not just policy failure.

6. [Construction starts on Egypt's first, Russian-built nuclear plant](https://www.brecorder.com/news/40187405/construction-starts-on-egypts-first-russian-built-nuclear-plant) - Reuters, July 22, 2022. Precise fact: first concrete was poured and construction began at El Dabaa after regulatory approval. Period fit: 1B infrastructure/capability context in 2022. Ruler attribution: flagship state project under El-Sisi. Limitations: project reporting does not establish broader performance.
